title: 법정 방청 및 촬영 등에 관한 규칙 / queue:ARTICLE:6:0:00006:part:1/1
title_original: 법정 방청 및 촬영 등에 관한 규칙
full_text:
Article 6 (Audio Recording, Video Recording and Filming for Broadcasting by Order of Presiding Judge)
(1) The presiding judge may order audio recording, video recording or filming for the purpose of broadcasting all or part of a trial or oral argument in any of the following cases:
1. Where the number of persons involved in the litigation significantly exceeds the capacity of the courtroom in which the proceedings are held and broadcasting is necessary to maintain courtroom order;
2. Where a disaster or comparable event has caused numerous casualties and a substantial number of the parties, victims, or their legal representatives (including spouses, lineal relatives, and siblings where the victim has died) live far from the court in which proceedings are held, making attendance in person difficult, and it is deemed appropriate for ensuring participation to enable them to watch the proceedings at a distant court equipped with broadcasting facilities.
(2) In the cases referred to in paragraph (1), the presiding judge may have audio recordings, video recordings or filmed footage broadcast at designated facilities as follows:
1. In a case under paragraph (1) 1: A facility within the court to which the presiding judge belongs;
2. In a case under paragraph (1) 2: A facility within the distant court.
(3) In a case under paragraph (2), prior approval shall be obtained as follows: <Amended on February 2, 2017.>
1. For a case under paragraph (2) 1: Approval from the president of the competent high court (including the president of the Patent Court) or the president of the district court (including the president of a Family Court, Administrative Court or Rehabilitation Court);
2. For a case under paragraph (2) 2: Approval from the Minister of the National Court Administration.
(4) The presiding judge may take measures necessary to prevent infringement of personal information of persons involved in litigation by the broadcasting.
